subject: Request: redwood penetration test summary & scope clarification (incident-adjacent)
messages:
From: Mike Turner <mike.turner@epsilonhealth.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: security@epsilonhealth.com, natasha.li@epsilonhealth.com
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 17:12:00 -0400
Subject: Unusual activity — request for penetration test report and scope

Hi Dylan,

We picked up an unusual series of API calls from one of our test services this morning that referenced a Redwood model endpoint. The incident itself appears contained on our side, but our security team has asked for the most recent penetration test report you can share (redacted as needed), plus a written note of the active scope for that test and whether the issue observed could be related to anything in scope. We are operating under a heightened posture due to a separate supply-chain notification and need to close out a mini-questionnaire for our risk committee by EOD Tuesday.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood performed a pen test that included the hosted inference endpoints in production in 2024–2025 window
- Which components were in scope (auth, control plane, runtime, telemetry, auditing)
- Whether there are known attack vectors or mitigations relevant to our observed calls (I can paste logs if helpful)

If you cannot share the full report, a redacted executive summary plus a signed attestation from your security team would suffice for our risk committee. Please advise acceptable next steps and any expected SLA for delivery.

Thanks,
Mike Turner
Head of Security Operations
Epsilon Health

(Attachment: incident_logs_excerpt.txt)

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@epsilonhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unusual activity — request for penetration test report and scope

Mike — thanks for flagging this and sharing the log excerpt. I appreciate the timeline constraint; we will treat this as an elevated request.

Quick answers up front:
- Yes — Redwood engaged an external pen testing firm in Nov 2024 that targeted both the hosted control plane and the inference runtime. The full test report contains exploit descriptions and specific IPs; we redact operational details for customer distribution.
- Scope included: authentication/authorization flows, control-plane APIs (model management, key provisioning), inference runtime surface (model RPC endpoints and ML-serving layer), and our telemetry/ingestion pipelines. Our customer-facing hosted endpoints were included in black-box testing.
- At a high level, none of the findings mapped to a persistent remote RCE against hosted inference endpoints; most findings were configuration or edge-auth issues that required mitigations (details below).

What I can provide now:
1) A redacted executive summary of the Nov 2024 pen test (PDF) and a one-page signed attestation from our Security team confirming scope and remediation status.
2) A SOC 2 snapshot that documents relevant control tests around change management and incident response (zipped).
3) A summary of the remediation steps completed in Q1 2025 and outstanding low-risk items with planned close dates.

I am copying Marissa (Customer Success) and Rishi (Security) to coordinate delivery and any targeted technical follow-up. If you can share the snippet of the raw logs you mentioned, Rishi can triage on specific indicators.

Proposed timeline:
- Today (Mon): Provide redacted executive summary + attestation + SOC 2 snapshot (by EOD PDT)
- Tue morning: Rishi to review logs and provide a written note on whether observed calls align with any known issues (deliver by 12:00 PM ET)

If that works, I will send the attachments and a short secure link for download.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Director, Account Success
Redwood Inference

(Attachments to follow: redwood_pen_test_summary_2024-11.pdf (redacted summary), redwood_soc2_snapshot_2025-09.zip)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@epsilonhealth.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Unusual activity — request for penetration test report and scope

Mike — I pushed the redacted summary and SOC 2 snapshot to a secure share and included an access checklist for your info. Link below (expires in 7 days):
https://redwood-secure.example.com/share/eps-20260504-pen-test

Attachments included in the share:
- redwood_pen_test_summary_2024-11.pdf (executive redaction; removes IPs, PoC code, client-specific data)
- evidence_access_instructions.txt (instructions for validating the signed attestation)
- redwood_soc2_snapshot_2025-09.zip (control test artifacts; PII removed)

Quick remediation summary: the critical/medium findings in Nov 2024 were addressed by Jan 2025 via configuration hardening, stricter token lifetimes, and additional egress filtering. Remaining low findings were scheduled for mitigations by Q2 2025 and related CVEs were patched on our runtime images. Rishi can confirm the specific fixes.

If you need the unredacted report under an NDA or a one-time viewing session with our pen-test vendor, we can arrange it — we typically require a commercial NDA and a time-limited, supervised review.

Let me know if the share link satisfies the committee; Dylan and I are available for a quick 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the findings.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: none — files uploaded to secure share)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@epsilonhealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 4 May 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unusual activity — request for penetration test report and scope

Mike — following up on the log snippet Dylan included: we reviewed the indicators you supplied and confirmed that the requests correspond to automated test harness traffic hitting a model-serving endpoint. There are no signatures of exploitation in the payloads you supplied (no known exploit patterns, no large payload exfiltration, and requests resolve within expected authentication windows).

Notes relevant to your committee:
- The Nov 2024 pen test covered the hosted inference endpoints under black-box conditions. Findings were categorized and remediated; the executive summary in the secure share documents remediation dates and risk ratings.
- We stand behind the remediation actions completed in Jan 2025; higher-risk items were validated internally and by the vendor.
- If your team requires the unredacted report for forensic correlation, we can provide a supervised review under NDA and a one-time non-disclosure addendum to our standard data handling agreement.

Requested next steps from Epsilon:
1) Confirm whether the redacted summary + attestation is acceptable for the risk committee.
2) If you require additional forensic correlation, provide a sanitized packet capture or additional logs and we will coordinate with the pen-test vendor.

If helpful I can add a short signed paragraph attesting to the remediation status and a brief risk statement summarizing open/closed findings.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Lead Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

(Inline: signed attestation placeholder — will attach PDF when final)
